title: unified-rollouts-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback-enhancements
author: Ethan Liu
release_notes: Enhancements to canary/AB/shadow autorollback workflows: add metric quorum and quarantine probing stage, tighten safety guards for rollback decisioning, improve telemetry and e2e stability tests.
description: Motivation: incidents in Q4 showed that single-metric rollbacks during high-variance workloads produced noisy autorollbacks and customer-facing disruptions. This PR implements multiple safety improvements to unified rollouts (canary / A/B / shadow): 1) metric quorum for autorollback decisions (requires majority agreement across configured metrics), 2) quarantine probing stage for unstable probes to avoid flapping, 3) extended cooldown windows and progressive weight decay for weighted canaries, 4) richer rollback telemetry and tracing hooks for faster investigation, and 5) new e2e stability tests to reduce regression risk. Changes are backward-compatible by default; feature gated under rollout.safety.v2 and enabled for internal canaries.

Performance: negligible overhead in evaluator path; added microbenchmark for quorum aggregator
performance_considerations: Metric quorum evaluator aggregates up to 8 metrics per rollout; microbenchmarks show <1ms median additional latency per decision on control-plane path
Telemetry payloads were flattened and sampled to avoid increased network cost; default sampling unchanged
Runtime inference paths unaffected; rollout decisions occur off the hot token path
rollback_behavior: Autorollback now requires configured metric quorum (default: majority of metrics) unless explicitly disabled
Quarantine stage pauses weight increases for probes marked unstable for a configurable window (default 60s)
Progressive decay reduces canary weight smoothly over configured decay window to avoid traffic spikes when rollback triggers
Manual override remains available via Console and API; rollbacks emit detailed reason and metric snapshots
rollout_plan: Feature gated under rollout.safety.v2 - enabled by default for internal/test clusters
Staged rollout to production: 10% of internal canaries -> 50% staging -> full production after 72h and no alerts
Post-merge: monitor rollback telemetry (dashboards added) and pause further rollouts if false-positive rate > 1% over 24h
